 There are a lot of aspects of Jayden Daniels' game that can be classed as eye-catching.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement When healthy, the Commanders hurler conjures up spectacles like few others at his position. The former LSU man is a menace in the open field, often using his speed and elusiveness to slip beyond opposition defenders. He can produce similar exploits in the pocket, picking teams apart with intricate passing, reading of the game and footwork.
 It's easy to see why the 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year has emerged as a fan favorite to those who drape themselves in burgundy-and-gold. It's not just his play that has people talking, however. It's also his attire — namely his helmet, which features a Japanese flag on its surface.
 Daniels is not a Japanese citizen to our knowledge. Yet, he sports the ensign proudly. Here's why.
 MORE: How elbow injuries have derailed Jayden Daniels' young NFL career 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Why Jayden Daniels wears a Japanese flag on his helmet
 Daniels' Japanese roots inspire his decision to sport the Hinomaru (circle of the sun in Japanese). His great-grandmother hails from the island nation, per the Associated Press — his mother's grandmother was born in Japan.
 Daniels previously sported just the U.S. flag decal on his helmet. In 2025, he added the Japanese flag to his repertoire. He uses the banner as a way to honor his great-grandmother.
 The San Bernardino, Calif. native first unveiled the insignia in the Commanders' season-opening win over the Giants in 2025. One year on, the look remains a signature part of his collection. He holds pride for the nation and its contributions to the world stage.
 You can expect to see him rocking it going forward during his NFL career.
